description:
FOUND s473t5e (#1501 round 6, `re/` CHECK 2).  t/re/reg_pmod.t is DIFF 58/30
and every one of its 30 blessed rows names one of the three caret variables:

    s/$r/p: ^MATCH is '345'          /$r/p: ^MATCH length
    s/345/p: ^PREMATCH is '012-'     s/$r/p: ^PREMATCH length
    s/345/p: ^POSTMATCH is '-6789'   /$r/p: ^POSTMATCH length

perl 5.10 added `/p` ("preserve"), which makes `${^MATCH}`, `${^PREMATCH}` and
`${^POSTMATCH}` hold what `$&`, `` $` `` and `$'` hold, for the match that was
compiled with it.  PCL has `$&`/`` $` ``/`$'` and none of the three caret
spellings.

ROWS: 30 blessed fail rows, one file.

SHAPE: PCL keeps the match data unconditionally (there is no
"copy the subject only under /p" optimisation to model), so the three variables
are ALIASES of the three punctuation ones and `/p` is a no-op modifier to
accept.  That makes this a small, self-contained runtime item: three magic
globals beside `$&` in the same table, each pipe-quoted (a caret variable of
any sigil must be -- DECIDED Â§s420), and `p` added to the accepted modifier
letters.

CHECK WHEN DOING IT: perl leaves the three UNDEF when the LAST successful match
was compiled WITHOUT /p, which an unconditional alias gets wrong in the other
direction; measure whether reg_pmod.t asserts that (it has rows named
"without /p") before choosing between the alias and a per-match flag.
subject: the `/p` modifier and `${^MATCH}` / `${^PREMATCH}` / `${^POSTMATCH}` are absent -- t/re/reg_pmod.t, 30 rows
